region: TTR and modern type theories: scoped comparisons
summary: MTT/DTS comparison through explicit noun translation: type liftings induce predicates; quantifiers agree on those images; negative predication does not require positive typing; the canonical donkey reading transfers only after packaging DTS predicate evidence into noun types.

sources.citation: Chatzikyriakidis, S. & Luo, Z. (2020). Formal Semantics in Modern Type Theories.
Bekki, D. & Mineshima, K. (2017). Context-Passing and Underspecification in Dependent Type Semantics.
sources.available: read: sections 1.1-1.4 and 3.1-3.3; title verified against PDF

definitions_mapped.note: Uses the existing common-supertype image rendering, not CL20's full heterogeneous IS.
Restricted to Prop-valued predicates; explicit induced Sigma noun types.

theorems.name: negative_predication / negative_predication_without_positive_typing
theorems.source_claim: Negative nominal predication is expressible without assuming positive membership.

theorems.name: donkey_after_noun_translation
theorems.source_claim: Canonical reading agreement after noun-ontology translation.

evidence: Assessment limited to the explicitly stated fragment; see audits/ttr_comparison.md. Mechanical results are stored separately in the .mech.json sidecar.
simplifications: No full heterogeneous IS, DTS @ calculus, proof search, or equivalence of arbitrary Type-valued predicates with Prop.
omissions: No full heterogeneous IS, DTS @ calculus, proof search, or equivalence of arbitrary Type-valued predicates with Prop.
